title: Blueprint Editor Tour 🗺️
description: Navigate the Event Graph, Components panel, and Details like a pro.

slides.title: The Editor Layout 🖼️
slides.content:
# Your Visual IDE

When you open a Blueprint, you enter a specialized editor with these main areas:

* **Toolbar** – Compile, Save, Play (Simulate)
* **Components Panel** (top‑left) – add and manage Components
* **My Blueprint Panel** (bottom‑left) – variables, functions, macros
* **Event Graph / Construction Script** (center) – the main graph canvas
* **Details Panel** (right) – properties of selected node or component

Switch between the **Event Graph** (runtime logic) and **Construction Script** (editor‑time setup) using the tabs at the top of the canvas.

quizData.question: Which panel lets you add new Components to your Blueprint?
quizData.explanation: The Components Panel shows the hierarchy of components and allows you to add new ones via the 'Add Component' button.

slides.title: Event Graph vs Construction Script 🔄
slides.content:
## Two Scripts for Two Purposes

* **Event Graph** – runs during gameplay. Contains events like BeginPlay, Tick.
* **Construction Script** – runs in the editor whenever the Blueprint is placed or modified. Use it to set up initial states.

Example: If you want a lamp to randomly choose a colour each time you drag it into a level, do it in the Construction Script. If you want the lamp to flicker during the game, use the Event Graph.

*Analogy:* Construction Script is the **factory setting**; Event Graph is the **day‑to‑day operation**.

quizData.question: The Construction Script runs when the game starts.
quizData.explanation: The Construction Script runs in the editor, during placement and editing. Event Graph handles gameplay events.

slides.title: Navigating the Graph 🖱️
slides.content:
## Move Around Like a Pro

* **Right‑click** – create nodes (context menu)
* **Left‑click drag** – select nodes
* **Middle‑mouse drag** – pan
* **Scroll wheel** – zoom
* **Ctrl+Scroll** – zoom faster
* **Ctrl+B** – find in Content Browser (the Blueprint asset)
* **F** – frame selected nodes
* **Home** – fit all nodes in view

Right‑click on an empty area to spawn a node. Start typing its name, and Unreal suggests matching nodes.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Search Bar is King

When right‑clicking, just start typing: 'Branch', 'Print', 'Delay'. Unreal will find the node instantly. No need to browse categories.
